chapters.title: Chapter 1: Cap Table Basics for Founders

lessons.title: Ownership Percentage vs Fully Diluted Ownership

children.text: Eighteen months after the angel round, TiffinBox closes a ₹4 crore seed round. Meera tells a friend she owns 37% of her company. The seed fund's investment memo says she owns 32%. Her lawyer says 32.88%. Nobody is lying. They are counting three different things, and only one of them is the number that decides what Meera takes home the day the company is sold.

body.text: Issued ownership tells you what exists today. Fully diluted ownership tells you what you will really own once every promise the company has made is kept. Founders should quote the second number and never be surprised by it.

children.text: Where TiffinBox Stands After the Seed Round

The seed fund invested ₹4 crore for 5,000 compulsorily convertible preference shares at ₹8,000 each. As part of the deal, the ESOP pool was topped up from 1,000 to 2,000 options. An early angel had also put in ₹32 lakh through a convertible note that has not yet converted. That is four kinds of claim on one company.

children.text: Percentages are rounded to two decimals, so the columns can add to 100.01%. Notice that Meera's share count never changes. Only the denominator moves: 16,250, then 18,250, then 18,750.

body.title: Issued vs fully diluted ownership at TiffinBox (%)

children.text: Issued shares = 6,000 + 4,000 + 1,250 + 5,000 = 16,250. Add the 2,000-option pool to get 18,250. Add the roughly 500 shares the convertible note becomes to get 18,750.

Meera on each basis: 6,000 ÷ 16,250 = 36.92%. 6,000 ÷ 18,250 = 32.88%. 6,000 ÷ 18,750 = 32.00%. The note conversion assumes ₹32,00,000 at a 20% discount to the ₹8,000 seed price, so ₹32,00,000 ÷ ₹6,400 = 500 shares. Chapter 3 covers how discounts and valuation caps decide that number.

body.text: When a term sheet says an investor will own 20% post-money, it almost always means 20% on a fully diluted basis, including an enlarged ESOP pool. If you model it on an issued basis, your own post-round stake will come out several points higher than reality. Ask in writing which basis the percentage uses and what pool size is assumed.

children.text: Which Number Do You Use When?

body.title: Issued basis vs fully diluted basis

columns.label: Use the issued basis for
points: Statutory records: the register of members and MCA filings
Counting who actually holds shares today
Checking share counts against Form PAS-3 and Form MGT-7
Dividend entitlement on shares already issued

columns.label: Use the fully diluted basis for
points: Negotiating any round and modelling your post-money stake
Working out what your shares are worth at an exit
Deciding ESOP grant sizes as a percentage of the company

body.text: Voting power follows a third path. Under Section 47 of the Companies Act, 2013, preference shareholders vote only on resolutions that directly affect their rights, or where their dividend has gone unpaid for two years or more. Investor control in Indian startups therefore comes mostly from the shareholders' agreement and the articles of association, through board seats and reserved matters, not from the raw percentage on the cap table. Chapter 4 takes this apart in detail.

body.label: The number that pays you
body.context: In a sale, liquidation preferences are paid first and the remainder is split on a fully diluted basis. A founder who tracks only the issued percentage will overestimate their exit proceeds twice over. Chapter 4 covers the preference stack.

body.title: Rohan on the strictest basis
body.prompt: Rohan holds 4,000 shares. Counting issued shares, the full 2,000-option ESOP pool and the roughly 500 shares the convertible note becomes, TiffinBox has 18,750 fully diluted shares. What is Rohan's fully diluted ownership? Answer to two decimal places.
body.explanation: 4,000 ÷ 18,750 × 100 = 21.33%. On an issued basis the same 4,000 shares read as 24.62%. The 3.29 percentage point difference is entirely made up of promises the company has already made to employees and the note holder.

body.title: Which basis answers the question?
body.question: An acquirer offers to buy TiffinBox. After all liquidation preferences are paid, the balance is divided among shareholders. Which ownership basis decides Meera's share of that balance?
options: The issued basis, because only issued shares are legally recognised
The fully diluted basis, because vested options are exercised and convertibles convert before the sale completes
Whichever basis is higher for the founder
Neither, because acquirers pay founders based on their role rather than their shareholding
body.explanation: Before an exit completes, option holders exercise their vested options and convertible instruments convert, so those shares genuinely exist by the time proceeds are split. That is why the fully diluted basis is the one that decides economics.

body.title: Name the basis
body.textWithBlank: Preference shares are usually counted in a cap table as if they had already turned into equity shares. This is called counting them on an as-___ basis.
body.explanation: CCPS are compulsorily convertible, so treating them as converted reflects the economics. The three columns in this lesson all count the seed fund's CCPS this way.

body.title: The 18% that was really 15%
body.scenario: A Gurugram D2C founder has 20,000 issued shares. A fund offers ₹6 crore for 18% of the company post-money, and the founder calculates that 18% of the enlarged company means about 4,390 new shares, leaving the two founders at roughly 68%. At closing, the lawyer's cap table shows the founders at 61%. The term sheet's fine print says the 18% is calculated on a fully diluted post-money basis and that a 12% ESOP pool must exist at closing. The company currently has no pool.
body.prompt: Why did the founders end up seven points lower, and what should they have asked for at term sheet stage?
body.modelAnswer:
Why the gap opened:
1. The founder modelled the round on an issued basis. The fund priced it on a fully diluted basis.
2. A 12% ESOP pool had to be created, and because the term sheet required it to exist at closing, the pool comes out of the pre-money company. In practice that means the existing shareholders, mostly the founders, absorb the whole of it.
3. The fund's 18% is protected. The pool is carved out of everyone else, so the founders take the hit rather than the new investor.

What to ask at term sheet stage:
1. Confirm in writing whether the investor's percentage is issued or fully diluted, and get one agreed cap table showing pre-round and post-round columns.
2. Ask what pool size is assumed and whether it is created pre-money or post-money. Pre-money dilutes only the existing holders; post-money dilutes the new investor too.
3. Justify the pool size with an actual 18-month hiring plan. A 12% pool for a company that needs 6% is a transfer of value from founders to the next round's optics.
4. Model your own stake three ways before signing: issued, fully diluted with the existing pool, and fully diluted with the required pool.

Chapter 3 covers this negotiation in full.

body.title: Quoting your ownership honestly
steps: Count issued shares across every class, including preference shares on an as-converted basis.
Add the entire ESOP pool, granted and ungranted.
Add every convertible note, iSAFE and warrant at its expected conversion, and state the assumption you used.
Divide your share count by that total to get your fully diluted percentage.
Keep both columns side by side in the cap table so nobody can quote the flattering number by accident.
Re-run the calculation before signing any term sheet, using the pool size the investor requires.

cards.definition: Ownership counted using only shares that have actually been allotted.
Ownership counted as if every option, warrant and convertible had already become equity shares.
Counting preference shares as though they had already converted into equity shares.
Compulsorily convertible preference shares, the instrument most Indian venture investors use.
Options set aside but not yet given to any employee. They still count in the fully diluted total.
An investor's ownership immediately after the round closes, almost always quoted on a fully diluted basis.

points: Issued ownership counts only allotted shares. Fully diluted ownership counts every share that will exist once options are exercised and convertibles convert.
Your share count stays fixed. Only the denominator grows, which is why your percentage falls.
At TiffinBox, Meera reads as 36.92% issued, 32.88% fully diluted with the pool, and 32.00% once the convertible note is included.
Term sheets quote percentages on a fully diluted basis, usually including an enlarged ESOP pool. Always confirm the basis and the assumed pool size in writing.
Exit proceeds are split on a fully diluted basis after liquidation preferences, so that is the number that decides what you are paid.
Voting power is a separate question governed by Section 47 of the Companies Act, 2013, the shareholders' agreement and the articles of association.
Keep both bases side by side in your cap table and quote the fully diluted number.

body.text: This lesson is for education only and is not legal, tax or investment advice. TiffinBox Foods and the other startups and people described are fictional, and all share counts, prices and conversion assumptions are illustrative. Conversion terms for notes and preference shares depend on the actual contract. Consult a qualified company secretary, chartered accountant or lawyer before relying on any cap table calculation.
